hook.text: The oldest known clothing is 170,000 years old—animal hides sewn with bone needles by early humans in Africa.

buildup.text: Clothing started as survival gear. Humans migrating out of Africa needed covering as temperatures dropped.

discovery.text: Lice DNA reveals clothing's age. Body lice diverged from head lice roughly when humans started wearing clothes.

twist.text: But tropical cultures also dress elaborately despite no cold. Clothing was never just about warmth—it was about meaning.

climax.text: From the first hide to the latest runway, every garment answers the same question: who do I want to be today?

punchline.text: We dressed for identity before we dressed for weather.
